skipped_revisions.author: safety_engineer
skipped_revisions.description: Reconciled the contactor reaction figures, which gave three different numbers for one chain: a 30 ms acceptance threshold, 35 ms in this record's own rationale and 40 ms in the safety goal's timing budget. Root cause was that 30 ms is the mechanical opening time alone - the value of FB2-PRM-000005 and FB2-ASM-006 - while the acceptance criterion it was attached to measures from the FAULT request to the FEEDBACK-open contactor, which additionally includes the coil command and the feedback confirmation. The chain was allocated in the safety goal as contactor_command 5 ms + contactor_mechanical 30 ms + feedback_verification 5 ms = 40 ms, and both the functional and the technical safety concept independently state that 40 ms is the end-to-end figure. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000024. Changes: (1) the 'Contactor open latency' threshold moves from 30 ms to 40 ms, because that criterion measures FAULT request to feedback open and 40 ms is what the allocated chain costs; (2) a new criterion 'Contactor mechanically open latency' is added at 35 ms for the FAULT request to mechanically open point, so the 30 ms mechanical parameter is no longer asked for under the wrong label; (3) the statement now distinguishes the mechanically open point (35 ms) from the feedback-confirmed point (40 ms); (4) the rationale is rewritten to state the full chain 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms and to say why the earlier 35 ms omitted the coil command. The coil de-energise criterion at 5 ms, the feedback-verification criterion and the weld-detection criterion are unchanged. No threshold was loosened to make a test pass: the 40 ms figure is the budget the record was already spending from, and adopting it makes the requirement harder to claim compliance with, not easier. The real foxBMS source was checked first and cannot settle the number - CONT_OpenContactor at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:165-182 requests the state change through SPS_RequestContactorState() and carries no timing constant - so the parameter registry FB2-PRM-000005 is the authority and it was not edited.

skipped_revisions.description: Separated this functional safety requirement (ISO 26262 Part 4) from FB2-HW-TSR-000004 (Part 5), which carried identical statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria, and made the shared 'All cells (or representative subset >= 50%)' coverage criterion measurable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000027. This record now states the safety intent and only acceptance criteria that a test can decide from the item's observable behaviour: that the reaction is retained while the main microcontroller is held in reset (100 percent of overvoltage test points), the independent detection latency of 50 ms, and the 50 mV threshold accuracy. The structural properties - which rails, references, driver stages and comparators are shared with the main chain, and how many cells the independent chain covers - are hardware design properties and now live only in FB2-HW-TSR-000004, which states the hardware obligation with its own hardware acceptance criteria. The coverage criterion is resolved to 100 percent of the cells the main measurement chain monitors: the 'representative subset >= 50%' branch was rejected because 'representative subset' is undefined, no selection method is recorded anywhere in the corpus, and a subset would leave cells with no barrier against a main-path failure, which is the barrier's purpose. The 100 percent figure follows the precedent already used by FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 ('All cell voltages acquired / Cell count match / 100 / %'). The feasibility of a full independent divider network is NOT asserted: FB2-ASM-008 already records it as 'Requires PCB space, separate power domain, additional BOM cost. Feasibility to be confirmed', and that assumption is unchanged by this revision. The ASIL (ASIL_B), the safety_goal_ref, the statement's 50 ms and the verification approach are unchanged. The 115 ms figure in the rationale was removed in the same revision under finding FB2-REV-FND-000026. Removed the 115 ms figure from the rationale and replaced it with arithmetic derived from the corpus's own parameter registry. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000026 reported 115 ms as appearing in no record; that part of its evidence is corrected here. The figure is real but stale: it is the sum of a superseded allocation recorded in FB2-REV-000001 (as_is vertical-slice review, embedded finding FB2-FND-000001) as 'FSR-001 specifies 10 Hz (100 ms); FSR-002 specifies 10 ms check; FSR-003 specifies 5 ms contactor; sum = 115 ms'. 100 + 10 + 5 = 115. The allocation has since changed - FB2-PRM-000003 now gives afe_acquisition_period_ms = 50 and FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 allocates 25 ms for acquisition - so the figure no longer describes anything in this corpus. The justification is now stated on figures that still hold: the main path is 85 ms of the 100 ms interval; at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the contactor chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms and the main path is 95 ms; and if detection waits one full acquisition period of FB2-PRM-000003 (50 ms) rather than the 25 ms allocated, the main path is 85 - 25 + 50 = 110 ms and overruns the interval. A main-path-only reaction therefore has no tolerance for a degraded contactor or for one acquisition period, which is the substantive argument for a second barrier and does not need the 115 ms. FB2-ASM-008's rationale carried the same stale figure and was corrected in the same pass.

skipped_revisions.description: Separated this functional safety requirement (ISO 26262 Part 4) from FB2-HW-TSR-000004 (Part 5), which carried identical statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria, and made the shared 'All cells (or representative subset >= 50%)' coverage criterion measurable. The structural properties - which rails, references, driver stages and comparators are shared with the main chain, and how many cells the independent chain covers - are hardware design properties and now live only in FB2-HW-TSR-000004, which states the hardware obligation with its own hardware acceptance criteria. The 105 ms total was NOT rounded down to 100 ms: the arithmetic now closes because 85 + 15 = 100, not because a number was adjusted to look equal. The 100 percent figure follows the precedent already used by FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 ('All cell voltages acquired / Cell count match / 100 / %'). The feasibility of a full independent divider network is NOT asserted: FB2-ASM-008 already records it as 'Requires PCB space, separate power domain, additional BOM cost. Feasibility to be confirmed', and that assumption is unchanged by this revision. The ASIL (ASIL_B), the safety_goal_ref, the statement's 50 ms and the verification approach are unchanged. The 115 ms figure in the rationale was removed in the same revision under finding FB2-REV-FND-000026. Removed the 115 ms figure from the rationale and replaced it with arithmetic derived from the corpus's own parameter registry. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000026 reported 115 ms as appearing in no record; that part of its evidence is corrected here. The figure is real but stale: it is the sum of a superseded allocation recorded in FB2-REV-000001 (as_is vertical-slice review, embedded finding FB2-FND-000001) as 'FSR-001 specifies 10 Hz (100 ms); FSR-002 specifies 10 ms check; FSR-003 specifies 5 ms contactor; sum = 115 ms'. 100 + 10 + 5 = 115.
